scope_limits: The primary fragment states no number or share of schoolyards.
The primary fragment states no deadline or mandate-end condition.
The primary fragment states no budget, target population, or measured outcome.
The broader all-neighbourhood formulation appears only in supporting interview evidence and is not imported into this commitment.

responsible_competence.rationale: The proposal appears in an authenticated Clermont-Ferrand municipal campaign context, but the competence link remains subject to evidence and methodological review.

components.implementation_state_rationale: The candidate programme mapping is unreviewed, the original scope and deadline are unstated, and competent completion evidence is incomplete.
components.decomposition_rationale: The primary wording expresses one independently assessable action. Splitting cooling, permeability, inclusion, co-design, site counts, or neighbourhood coverage into campaign components would import details from later sources and alter the original commitment.
limitations: Plural wording establishes more than one schoolyard only at a linguistic level; it does not define a numerical target.
No mandate-end deadline is inferred from the fragment.
Programme outputs, outcomes, and impacts remain separate from this campaign component.

scope_comparison.rationale: Both records concern municipal action in Clermont-Ferrand. Compatibility does not by itself prove programme continuity.

scope_comparison.programme_scope: Ecological, cooler, permeable, inclusive, and co-designed transformation of schoolyards
scope_comparison.rationale: The adopted programme includes schoolyard greening but defines a broader transformation. Its additional properties are not retroactively attributed to the campaign wording.

scope_comparison.commitment_scope: No number, proportion, or denominator stated
scope_comparison.programme_scope: Later programme targets exist in separate sources but are not used as campaign targets
scope_comparison.rationale: No compatible campaign denominator exists, so a delivery ratio or numerical fulfillment test cannot be constructed.
A later policy period cannot silently become the campaign commitment deadline.

scope_comparison.commitment_scope: Plural schoolyards; no all-neighbourhood or complete-city coverage in the primary fragment
scope_comparison.programme_scope: Municipal programme with multiple school sites
scope_comparison.rationale: The sources share a municipal setting, but the primary wording provides no compatible site universe or geographic denominator.

scope_comparison.commitment_scope: Proposal attributed to Olivier Bianchi and Naturellement Clermont
scope_comparison.programme_scope: Policy adopted and implemented by the Ville de Clermont-Ferrand
scope_comparison.rationale: Campaign attribution and municipal policy adoption are evidenced separately, but a first-class evidence fragment directly documenting continuity remains to be acquired or reviewed.

scope_comparison.commitment_scope: Campaign page captured in 2019 before the 2020 municipal election
scope_comparison.programme_scope: Later programme action and adopted policy records
scope_comparison.rationale: The sequence is compatible with implementation, but chronology alone does not establish that the programme implements the promise.

mapping.rationale: The authenticated campaign proposal and adopted policy concern compatible schoolyard-greening action in the same municipal territory. The adopted programme is broader and later. This supports a candidate implementation mapping only; direct continuity, complete scope equivalence, delivery, fulfillment, outcomes, and impact remain unverified.

limitations: The bounded corpus is not exhaustive, so no identified counterevidence is not evidence that none exists.
Differently scoped programme targets are not treated as contradictions with an unquantified primary fragment.
Shared subject matter is insufficient by itself; institutional continuity still requires review.
The mapping does not establish that every programme activity derives from the campaign proposal.
The mapping does not establish a numerical target, deadline, delivery state, fulfillment conclusion, outcome, or causal impact.

evidence_references.locator: HTML content block under the heading “Végétalisation” on the archived “Une ville nature” page
printed page 25, Respire à la récré inset

uncertainty.explanation: The programme includes schoolyard greening but also contains broader design and policy objectives absent from the campaign fragment.
No retained first-class fragment directly states that Respire à la récré implements this campaign proposal.
The campaign fragment has no numerical, population, neighbourhood, or deadline scope suitable for complete comparison.
The chronology is compatible with continuity, but chronological sequence is not direct mapping evidence.
Competent works-acceptance records have not been located for the selected sites or complete programme scope.

notes: Maintainer approval authorized preparation of this bounded proposal; it did not constitute methodological acceptance.
A reviewer must decide whether the converging context is sufficient or whether direct continuity evidence is required before accepting the mapping.
Any accepted review must record role, decision, timestamp, rationale, reviewed version, counterevidence, and limitations.

prohibited_inferences: Do not infer a numerical target or completion ratio.
Do not attribute the all-neighbourhood formulation to the primary fragment.
Do not treat later programme objectives as original campaign wording.
Do not assign a public fulfillment conclusion from this proposed mapping.
Do not infer outcomes or causal impact from programme delivery evidence.
